Apple is rumored to be launching a brand-new MacBook Ultra this fall, as part of its ever-expanding "Ultra" product line. Here are six new features expected from the MacBook Ultra.

#1: A brand-new design that's thinner and lighter than the MacBook Pro

Bloomberg points out that Apple's new MacBook model is a "complete redesign," thinner and lighter than the current MacBook Pro.

The MacBook Ultra was originally expected to launch under the "MacBook Pro" branding, but with an all-new design. This could change at any time, but for now the rumors point to the "Ultra" branding.

We don't know whether the ports will be reduced compared to the MacBook Pro, but it's very possible. I'd be surprised if Apple pushed the "thin and light" angle too far, since the MacBook Ultra will likely appeal to a lot of Pro users.

#2: M5 Pro and M5 Max chips

The outside world has long expected the brand-new M6 chip series to make its debut with the MacBook Ultra. But recent rumors tell a different story.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports that Apple has shelved plans for the M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, and has instead accelerated development of a high-performance M7 chip.

Therefore, while a future MacBook Ultra will feature those M7 chips, this year's model is reportedly sticking with the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips from the MacBook Pro.

#3: Touch screen—a first for the Mac lineup

Touch support is coming to the Mac, and the MacBook Ultra will be the first model to feature a touch screen.

According to Mark Gurman, Apple is adding touch to the Mac as a supplementary input method, not as a replacement for the keyboard and trackpad.

macOS Golden Gate comes with several optimizations, offering interface elements that make touch operation more convenient, while still working well for users without a touch screen.

#4: OLED display

Every iPhone now uses an OLED display, and the iPad Pro also got an excellent tandem OLED in 2024. But the Mac has always been the exception—until now.

The MacBook Ultra will adopt OLED, becoming the first Mac to feature this display technology.

OLED can deliver purer blacks, better contrast, and wider viewing angles. It may also help the MacBook Ultra achieve longer battery life.

#5: Dynamic Island

The 2021 MacBook Pro was the first Mac to feature the "notch," but the MacBook Ultra will drop this design.

The all-new MacBook Ultra is expected to ditch the "notch" in favor of a punch-hole camera cutout, and add a new software feature: Dynamic Island.

Just like on the iPhone, Dynamic Island uses software to mask the camera cutout while providing new practical features for macOS—including serving as the home for Siri AI.

Big if true #6: Cellular connectivity with the C2 modem

Apple has yet to launch a Mac with cellular connectivity. But rumors suggest that may be about to change.

Mark Gurman wrote in a late-2024 report on Apple's in-house cellular modem plans:

Of course, there's no guarantee at all that this is the year the Mac gets cellular connectivity. But with Apple's C2 modem set to debut this fall alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, the timing seems just right.

Which new feature of the MacBook Ultra are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
